assertion.objects: The actual rank-two Tate lattice T2(E), its perfect alternating Weil pairing and its Galois action.
assertion.hypotheses: E/Q is the fixed characteristic-zero elliptic curve; the integral cyclotomic Weil pairing is perfect.
assertion.quantifiers: Every finite coefficient stage i and all vectors in the stated modules.
assertion.uniformity: Compatible with the multiplication maps defining the Tate inverse limit.
assertion.normalizations: Cyclotomic character on Z2(1); determinant of the original Tate action, before any scalar twist.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No assertion for torsion order divisible by positive characteristic; no generic-isogeny pairing remark is used.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the perfect alternating Tate pairing, then compare its Galois transformation with the rank-two determinant.
assertion.statement: The determinant of the actual Tate representation is the2-adic cyclotomic character.

use.reason: The rank-two pairing identity determines the determinant character used in the cyclotomic-kernel argument.

supplier.statement: Finite Weil pairings are bilinear, alternating, nondegenerate and Galois equivariant; their compatible inverse limit gives the corresponding Tate-module pairing.

publication.title: The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves
publication.locator: III Section8 Proposition8.1(a)–(e),p94; compatible inverse limit and Proposition8.3,pp97–98
publication.corrections: Published8.1(b) proof correction G^m=F composed with[m] retained; generalized-isogeny remark unused.

available_assertion.objects: An elliptic curve E/K, its finite m-torsion and l-adic Tate module, with roots of unity as pairing target.
available_assertion.hypotheses: m>=2 is prime to char(K); l is a prime distinct from char(K).
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every such elliptic curve, every such finite m and prime l; all torsion or Tate-module vectors and all Galois elements.
available_assertion.uniformity: Compatible with the multiplication maps defining the Tate inverse limit.
available_assertion.normalizations: Cyclotomic Galois action on roots of unity and Z_l(1); alternating pairing, not an untwisted scalar-valued Galois invariant form.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No assertion for torsion order divisible by positive characteristic; no generic-isogeny pairing remark is used.
available_assertion.limit_order: Form compatible finite torsion pairings before passing to the Tate module.
available_assertion.statement: Finite Weil pairings are bilinear, alternating, nondegenerate and Galois equivariant; their compatible inverse limit gives the corresponding Tate-module pairing.

adverse_cases.reason: For a basis with unit pairing value, e(gv,gw)=det(g)e(v,w), while Galois equivariance gives chi_cyc(g)e(v,w). Cancel the unit. This uses the original two-dimensional Tate lattice and gives no statement about arbitrary twisted determinants.
